content.title: Croatia beat Colombia 2-1 in World Cup warm-up | Reuters
content.text: Skip to main contentReport AdExclusive news, data and analytics for financial market professionalsLearn more aboutRefinitivFeedbackORLANDO, Florida, March 26 (Reuters) - Croatia secured a 2-1 win over Colombia in a ​World Cup warm-up match on ‌Thursday, overturning an early deficit with goals from Luka Vuskovic and Igor Matanovic.Jhon ​Arias put Colombia ahead in the ​third minute, his deflected shot beating ⁠Croatian goalkeeper Ivica Ivusic after ​a smart back heel from Luis ​Suarez.The Reuters Iran Briefing newsletter keeps you informed with the latest developments and analysis of the Iran war. Sign up here.Croatia responded three minutes later when Vuskovic scored a brilliant equaliser from outside the box, ​his shot bouncing off the ​post and into the net.Croatia completed the turnaround ‌in ⁠the 42nd minute after Colombian goalkeeper Camilo Vargas misjudged a high ball and Matanovic capitalised on the mistake, ​heading into ​the ⁠bottom corner.Colombia are drawn in Group K for the ​June 11 to July 19 ​World ⁠Cup in North America alongside Portugal, Uzbekistan and a playoff winner, while Croatia ⁠are ​in Group L ​with England, Ghana and Panama.Reporting by Angelica Medina ​in Mexico City; Editing by Peter Rutherford Our Standards: The Thomson Reuters Trust Principles., opens new tabXFacebookLinkedinEmailLinkPurchase Licensing RightsRead Next6 hours agoSoccerDenmark enter period of transition after missing 2026 World Cup6 hours agoSoccerBarcelona brush aside Real Madrid to make Women's Champions League semis1 hour agoSoccerDe Zerbi commits to stay at Spurs next season regardless of results9 hours agoRugbyFrance's Bielle-Biarrey named Six Nations Player of the Championship12 hours agoSoccerLewandowski hints at Poland exit after playoff heartbreak5 hours agoSoccerLego to continue sports expansion with soccer playersSportsAuburn drubs Illinois State, will face Tulsa in NIT finalBasketballcategory · April 2, 2026 · 11:05 PM CDT · 18 mins agoKeyshawn Hall was nearly unstoppable in a 24-point outing for overall No. 1 seed Auburn, and the sharp-shooting Tigers walloped Illinois State 88-66 in Thursday night's second NIT semifinal ​in Indianapolis.NHLcategoryOilers run win streak to 5 with defeat of Blackhawks22 mins agoSportscategoryUNC target Tommy Lloyd: 'Full focus' on Arizona, Final Four30 mins agoRugbyFormer rugby league great Glover dies aged 7037 mins agoBasketballcategoryWest Virginia edges Stanford in OT to advance to semifinals in Vegas1 hour ago Subscribe to Reuters to continue reading.Final price$1per weekPlus applicable taxes.
